Sample.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/8] We randomly assigned 408 middle school students (ages 10-15) to one of three conditions: PRP-A, PRP-AP (in which adolescents participated in PRP-A and parents were invited to attend a parent intervention component), or a school-as-usual control.

IPT.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/8] Method—We evaluated the effectiveness of the Penn Resiliency Program for adolescents (PRP-A), a school-based group intervention that targets cognitive behavioral risk factors for depression. [/page/1/Text/10] Conclusion—These findings suggest that cognitive-behavioral interventions can be beneficial when delivered by school teachers and counselors. [/page/2/Text/7] The Penn Resiliency Program (PRP), which is the focus of this research, is a CB intervention for young adolescents that is intended for delivery in schools.

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/7] Objective—Depression is a common psychological problem in adolescence. Recent research suggests that group cognitive-behavioral interventions can reduce and prevent symptoms of depression in youth. [/page/1/Text/8] Method—We evaluated the effectiveness of the Penn Resiliency Program for adolescents (PRP-A), a school-based group intervention that targets cognitive behavioral risk factors for depression. [/page/1/Text/9] We found no intervention effects on clinical levels of depression or anxiety. [/page/2/Text/7] The Penn Resiliency Program (PRP), which is the focus of this research, is a CB intervention for young adolescents that is intended for delivery in schools. PRP is one of the most widely researched depression prevention programs. It has been tested as a targeted intervention, with high risk youth, and as a universal intervention.

Source.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/8] Adolescents completed measures of depression and anxiety symptoms, cognitive style, and coping at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at 6-month follow-up.

MedCat.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/8] Adolescents completed measures of depression and anxiety symptoms, cognitive style, and coping at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at 6-month follow-up. [/page/1/Text/9] Among participants with average and high levels of hopelessness, PRP (A and AP) significantly improved depression symptoms, anxiety symptoms, hopelessness, and active coping relative to control.
